doc.citation: Wellman, C.H., Steemans, P. and Lopes, G. (2023). Dispersed spore assemblages from the Lower Devonian Rañeces - La Vid groups of Northern Spain: Palaeogeographical implications. Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 310, 104825.
doc.comment: Valporquero is extracted at formation scope because Sections 5.7 and 6 explicitly treat its samples as a single assemblage; its sample distributions are in Tables 4–6. Caption-only and table-only records are retained. Checklist counts, table entries, caption identifications and some sample codes disagree. Appendix A lists 40 Valporquero samples versus 39 in Section 5.7, and five La Pedrosa samples at L13 versus six in Section 5.6. Reworking is discussed but considered unsupported. Table 1 reprises historical records separately: principally Cramer (1967), with additional 1969 and Cramer and Diez (1976) records; the paper inconsistently cites Cramer 1967a and 1967b. These are literature records, not demonstrated reuse of specimens. Table 7 is a bibliographic inventory of external assemblages without occurrence lists. Coladilla was examined but not sampled; the two Cremenes samples have no formation or recovery information.

items.notes: Explicitly treated as a single assemblage in Sections 5.7 and 6.1. Marine palynomorphs dominate; spores vary from rare to abundant. No single coordinate represents this geographically distributed assemblage; Appendix A gives sample coordinates. Barren Valporquero samples listed there are 00-C623-5, 00-C623-6, 00-C623-7, 17SPAIN37, 17SPAIN38, 17SPAIN39, 00LV03, 17SPAIN44, 17SPAIN45 and 18SPAIN04; other unlogged recoveries include rare or coalified spores without identifications. The authors report 62 taxa, but generic pools, table-only taxa and caption-only morphotypes prevent treating the occurrence count here as that species total. Table 4 adds Dibolisporites wetteldorfensiS and Brochotriletes hudsonii, absent from Table 2. Table 2 uses Brochotriletes foveolatus, while distribution tables print Brochosporites; Table 4 prints Ambitisporires sp. A, and Tables 4 and 6 print Cirratriradites diaphanous. Alternative printed spellings are not counted as additional taxa here. Table 6 labels the L7 sample 17/35, whereas Appendix A and Fig. 4 give 18SPAIN35; Plate IV.1 and Plate VII.4 cite 17SPAIN35. Plate I spells divellomedium while Table 2 and distribution tables use divellomedia. Table 2 has several incorrect plate cross-references; occurrence locators below follow the actual captions. Unusual age ranges are interpreted as possible local range extensions, with little evidence of reworking; characteristic underlying San Pedro spores such as Iberoespora are absent.

items.age_basis_detail: Historical records assigned collectively to the Rañeces - La Vid groups; the reviewed groups span late Lochkovian to late Emsian, but Table 1 gives no taxon-specific levels.
items.notes: Secondary historical compilation, separate from the new collections. Earlier work primarily concerned marine palynomorphs. Table 1 reproduces original taxon names and proposes modern determinations; those determinations are not added as extra historical occurrences. Earlier illustrations are cited in Table 1 but are not reproduced as illustrations of these historical specimens here. The anomalous combined cf.? identification is retained verbatim, with cf. in the single-valued qualifier field. Section 3 calls the principal source Cramer (1967b), whereas the introduction and Table 7 cite Cramer (1967a), Palynology of Silurian and Devonian rocks in Northwest Spain. Table 1 also cites 1969 and 1976 illustrations; Cramer and Diez (1976), Acritarchs from the La Vid Shales (Emsian to lower Couvinian) at Colle, Leon, Spain, is listed in the references.
